response.hypothesis: Reduce to min-cost circulation: add a virtual arc sink->source with lower=upper=amount, cost 0. Self-loops don't affect conservation, so each contributes upper*cost if cost<0 else lower*cost, in closed form. For every remaining edge, pick the base flow f0 at a bound (f0=lower if cost>=0, f0=upper if cost<0) and represent the remaining freedom by a single residual arc of capacity upper-lower whose cost is |cost| >= 0 (forward u->v with cost c, or backward v->u with cost -c for saturated negative edges). Cost(f) = base + cost(residual flow) exactly, and the leftover problem is a b-flow: node v with divergence d(v)=out-in must receive -d(v). Attach a super-source to deficit nodes and super-sink to surplus nodes and run successive-shortest-paths min-cost max-flow with Dijkstra + Johnson potentials (valid since all residual costs are nonnegative; stale potentials on unreachable nodes stay consistent because any residual arc into an unreachable node comes from an unreachable node). Feasible iff the max flow saturates all supplies; answer = base + selfloop + flow cost, else null.
